frameworkAgreement.description:
The successful Tenderer will enter into a Framework Agreement (NEPO219 - Building Materials and Managed Stores) with NEPO & TPPL. This Framework will be made accessible to the Member Authorities and the Associate Members of NEPO and TPPL via Call-Off contracts. NEPO will establish overarching terms and conditions that define the core principles of the Framework.
Pricing will be determined through the tender process and evaluated against predefined award criteria and associated weightings. All tenderers will be assessed accordingly.
Pricing submitted as part of this Framework will apply to requirements nationally.
Contracting Authorities may establish Call-Off contracts through either Direct Award or Mini/Further Competition. A Direct Award may be used where the Contracting Authority objectively determine that there are benefits and rationale, this rationale may include but is not limited to: necessity for urgency relating to timescales, the complexity of the project or continuity of works.
This is subject to the Contracting Authority's internal procurement and legal guidelines permitting a Direct Award.
A basket of goods for each lot will be evaluated at framework level. This does not limit Contracting Authorities from accessing this lot of the Framework to purchase goods not covered by the pricing schedule. 
Contracting Authorities may utilise one or more pricing methodologies available under the Framework, including fixed pricing arrangements, basket pricing models, schedule of rates, project-specific pricing, Open Book arrangements and Return on Sales (ROS) commercial models.
All suppliers awarded to the Framework may be invited to participate in Further Competitions. The evaluation criteria for any Further Competitions will be specified by the Contracting Authority and included in the competition documentation. Suppliers will be required to submit pricing based on the specific project requirements.
NEPO and TPPL may, during the term of the Framework Agreement, make available digital tools, applications or technology solutions designed to assist Contracting Authorities in identifying Supplier locations, product availability and other operational information. Suppliers should cooperate with reasonable requests to support such initiatives where they are capable of doing so. Participation in such initiatives shall not be mandatory unless otherwise agreed between the parties.

tender.title: Peatland ACTION FW02 Field Ecologists Framework
tender.description:
NatureScot work to improve our natural environment in Scotland and inspire everyone to care more about it. We work to ensure that all nature in Scotland - our key habitats and landscapes, all our green space and our native species - are maintained, enhanced and bring us benefits. Our priority is a nature-rich future for Scotland and an effective response to the climate emergency.
Peatland ACTION funding - from Scottish Government - primarily supports on-the-ground peatland restoration activities and is open for applications from eligible land managers who have peatlands that would benefit from restoration. There are no geographical restrictions or target areas for Peatland ACTION funding. Peatlands are an iconic part of the Scottish landscape and have many benefits for people and nature. Healthy peatlands provide important ecosystem services including storing and sequestering carbon, supporting unique and specialised biodiversity, improving downstream water quality, and regulating water flow to provide natural flood management. In contrast, damage to peatlands reduces or reverses these benefits. For example, degraded peatlands release stored carbon and are a major global source of greenhouse gas emissions.
Peatland ACTION is led and funded by Scottish Government and delivered in partnership with NatureScot, Cairngorms National Park Authority, Loch Lomond & the Trossachs National Park Authority, Forestry and Land Scotland, and Scottish Water.
Since 2012, Peatland ACTION has set over 66,000 hectares of degraded peatland on the road to recovery, but this effort needs to accelerate rapidly in the coming years to help address the twin crises of the climate emergency and biodiversity loss.
The appointed Field Ecologists will work with the Peatland ACTION Technical Team and Project Officers located across Scotland to help support species and ecological survey requirements for Peatland ACTION restoration sites.

lots.description:
The primary role for the appointed Field Ecologists will be to carry out protected species surveys on request, which may include surveys for breeding birds (including Schedule 1 species), raptor roosts, mammals, freshwater pearl mussel, reptiles, or plants.
Field Ecologists must be suitably skilled and experienced in carrying out a range of species surveys of this nature. Surveys conducted prior to peatland restoration work commencing on site will be used to plan the restoration work and ensure all project personnel (agents, contractors / workers) are aware of the presence of any protected species on site and any mitigation and licensing requirements.
Surveys conducted during restoration works will also be used to provide continued ecological support to project personnel, including mitigation requirements, safe working distances/buffer zones, preparation of species protection plans and may include giving toolbox talks. Additional information: Scotland Excel is acting on behalf of NatureScot in the execution of this tender but will not be party to the contract or the management of the contract throughout its lifetime.

tender.title: Heating, Electrical, Mechanical and Decarbonisation Framework
tender.description: The procurement will establish a single combined, multi-supplier Heating, Electrical, Mechanical and Decarbonisation Framework, not divided into lots, for the provision of works and associated services to domestic and non-domestic properties and buildings, including occupied and void properties. The scope will include, but is not limited to, the provision, supply, installation, replacement, upgrading, servicing, statutory and safety inspection, testing, planned and responsive maintenance and repair of heating, electrical, mechanical, renewable, low-carbon and associated energy systems. Heating works and services will include domestic and commercial/communal systems and equipment using gas, oil, solid fuel, electricity and renewable or low-carbon technologies, including gas and oil boilers, electric storage and panel heaters, electric low-pressure hot water boilers, air source heat pumps, solar-assisted heat pumps, ground source heat pumps, biomass boilers, combined heat and power and micro-CHP systems, heat networks, solar thermal systems, microgeneration installations, wind turbines and other emerging renewable heating and energy technologies. Associated heating and hot-water systems may include hot and cold water services, vented and unvented hot-water cylinders, oil storage tanks, flues, pumps, filling loops, pipework, radiators, low-surface-temperature radiators, fan convectors, controls, smart thermostats and associated electrical controls, together with pipework system cleaning, flushing, de-sludging, de-scaling, sterilisation, water treatment and pipe insulation. The framework will include annual heating safety checks and servicing, Landlord safety and compliance requirements, servicing and maintenance of thermostatic mixing valves and unvented cylinders, planned and responsive repairs, breakdown services, replacement of defective components and systems, void and mutual-exchange checks and emergency and out-of-hours attendance, including 24-hour, 365/366-day services where required. Electrical works and services will include complete and partial rewiring, upgrading, alteration, inspection, testing, certification, Electrical Installation Condition Reports and associated remedial works; consumer units and distribution equipment; RCBOs, RCDs/RCCBs, AFDDs and surge protection devices; main service intake works and associated DNO requirements; earthing and bonding; power, lighting and final circuits; sockets, switches and appliance supplies; immersion heaters; electric showers; connections to heating and boiler systems; external and communal/landlord lighting; supplies to outbuildings and external stores; extract fans and ventilation-related electrical works; doorbells; TV aerial cabling and outlets; photocells, time switches and lighting controls; and associated electrical equipment and systems. The electrical scope will also include domestic fire detection and smoke, heat and carbon-monoxide alarm systems and associated equipment, including interconnection and radio-frequency equipment, together with servicing, maintenance and responsive repair of electric heating installations and 24-hour breakdown provision. Electric vehicle charging infrastructure may be supplied and installed, including associated equipment and services required to provide fully operational charging installations. Mechanical works and services will include mechanical ventilation with heat recovery systems and associated equipment, thermostatic mixing valves, boosted cold-water pump installations and other mechanical equipment associated with heating, hot water, ventilation and energy systems, including servicing and maintenance where required. The decarbonisation and energy scope will include solar photovoltaic systems and associated services, including inverters, controls, metering, monitoring and battery storage systems, together with solar thermal, air source heat pumps, ground source heat pumps, solar-assisted heat pumps, biomass, CHP/micro-CHP, heat networks, wind turbines, mechanical ventilation with heat recovery, smart heating controls, sensors and monitoring equipment and other emerging renewable, low-carbon and energy-efficiency technologies associated with the heating, electrical, mechanical and decarbonisation scope that may be required during the life of the framework. The framework may support retrofit, decarbonisation, ventilation, overheating, indoor-air-quality, EPC improvement, net-zero and future energy-performance requirements, including requirements arising from grant-funded programmes. Retrofit assessment, energy and technical support services may include pre- and post-works Energy Performance Certificates, energy assessments, SAP10 assessments, retrofit assessments, retrofit coordination, retrofit design, PAS 2035 site visits, air-pressure testing, technical monitoring and cavity-wall borescope services, together with associated services. Legionella risk assessments may also be instructed where required in connection with the works and systems covered by the framework. Project management services may be provided for heating, electrical, mechanical, retrofit and decarbonisation programmes, including grant-funded programmes, and may include management and coordination of the appointed supplier's own works and/or coordination of works delivered in collaboration with other framework suppliers. Requirements may be delivered as individual property works, grouped schemes, planned programmes, servicing and compliance programmes, responsive repairs, emergency works, grant-funded projects and larger retrofit or decarbonisation programmes, together with associated services. The framework is intended to remain sufficiently flexible to respond to changes in legislation, technical standards, funding requirements and technology during its term, including the introduction of emerging renewable and energy-efficiency measures falling within the heating, electrical, mechanical and decarbonisation scope. Suppliers appointed to the framework, either directly or through their declared supply chain, will be required to have the capability to deliver the overall range of works and services included within the scope.

tender.title: Control Software
tender.description: For this project We have 6 modules. Each module is made up of 3 stages. These stages are (1) an x-y stage, (2) a tilt goniometric stage, and (3) rotational stage. The links to these stages and the control box can be seen in the attached supporting document. The difference between our stages and the COTS stages is that each stage has a different motor to the COTS item (integrated 485 bus-type closed-loop stepper driver, IRS42E-K02, manual available). All modules are controlled via a single controller box. The controller box has power and user instructions from control software (via RS232 to USB cable) as inputs and has six output cables, each connected to one of the modules (RS232 to RS232). Each output cable is limited to 2m length. The cable from the controller connects to the bottom most stage of the module, that is the x-stage. The x-stage is then connected to the y-stage via a RS232 cable. The y-stage is connected to the goniometric stage via a RS232 cable. Finally, the goniometric stage is connected to the rotational stage via a RS232 cable. In this way, a controller with 6 outputs controls 6x4=24 motors. This setup is shown in the diagram and a picture of a single module is also provided on the attached supporting document. The control signal is sent via the control box to the desired module. If the control signal is not for the x-stage, the control signal is passed up the chain, and so on. We need the control software to interface with our existing hardware to control the 6 modules. The solution could interface with the existing control box, or alternatively provide a new controller to interface with the 6 modules. The requirements above are for the software/control of the 6 modules.

milestones.description:
South Gloucestershire Council (SGC) is conducting a Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise in relation to its procurement of Temporary Traffic Management services to assist it in developing its requirements and approach.
This engagement is conducted in accordance with Section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023, which permits contracting authorities to engage with the market prior to commencing a procurement procedure.
The purpose of this PME is to:
• Understand market capacity and interest.
• Check and develop procurement requirements.
• Help design procedures, participation conditions and award criteria.
• Identify any potential barriers to participation.
SGC is sharing *DRAFT* Invitation to Tender (ITT) documentation and seeking feedback from the market on the information contained therein.
Participation in this PME is voluntary, but SGC encourages any organisation or group of organisations interested in bidding for this contract to respond to the questions contained within it's 'Preliminary Market Engagement Questionnaire'. Your feedback is valuable in helping us shape a fair, transparent and effective procurement process.
SGC are still finalising their approach and documentation. The responses to its PME Questionnaire will be fed into this process and the finished tender documents are anticipated to be issued shortly after the engagement deadline.
PLEASE NOTE: The e-sender form for the completion of this UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement Notice does not give the option for SGC to specify the closing time for the return of responses. We believe this will display on the notice as 23:59, but the Council asks please that PME Questionnaire responses are returned by 17:00 on Friday 25 September 2026.
